body_html:
What rounding means

Rounding finds the closest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 or 100,000. Rounded numbers are easier to work with, and they help you check whether an answer makes sense.

The rounding rule

  1. Find the digit in the place you are rounding to.
  2. Look at the digit one place to its right.
  3. 5 or more: round up (add 1 to the rounding digit). 4 or less: round down (keep it).
  4. Change every digit to the right of the rounding place to 0.
Round 548,362 to the nearestLook atAnswer
10the ones digit: 2548,360
100the tens digit: 6548,400
1,000the hundreds digit: 3548,000
10,000the thousands digit: 8550,000
100,000the ten thousands digit: 4500,000
Exactly halfway

Round 465,000 to the nearest 10,000.

465,000 is exactly halfway between 460,000 and 470,000. A number that is exactly halfway rounds up.

Answer: 470,000

Watch the 9s

Round 396,500 to the nearest 10,000.

The ten thousands digit is 9 and the thousands digit is 6, so round up. 9 ten thousands + 1 ten thousand = 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand: 390,000 + 10,000 = 400,000.

Answer: 400,000

Estimating with rounding

Round each number first, then add or subtract the rounded numbers. If your exact answer is far from the estimate, check your working.

Estimate

Estimate 59,820 + 21,350 by rounding to the nearest 1,000.

59,820 rounds to 60,000 and 21,350 rounds to 21,000. 60,000 + 21,000 = 81,000. The exact answer, 81,170, is close.

Answer: about 81,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding 465,000 down to 460,000Exactly halfway rounds up: 470,000
Rounding the wrong place (548,362 to the nearest 10,000 = 548,000)Find the ten thousands digit first: 550,000
Keeping the digits after the place (34,628 → 35,628)Change every digit after the place to 0: 35,000
Writing 10 in one place (695,000 → 6,100,000) or losing it (695,000 → 600,000)Exchange 10 ten thousands for 1 hundred thousand: 700,000
Rounding twice (645,380 → 650,000 → 700,000)Always round the original number: 600,000

faq.q: What rounding do Year 5 children learn?
faq.a: The National Curriculum says Year 5 pupils should round any number up to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000. They also round decimals to the nearest whole number and to one decimal place.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest 10,000?
faq.a: Look at the thousands digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. So 46,800 rounds to 50,000 and 43,900 rounds to 40,000.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest 100,000?
faq.a: Look at the ten thousands digit. 5 or more rounds up and 4 or less rounds down, so 258,000 rounds to 300,000 and 349,999 rounds to 300,000.

faq.q: How do you teach rounding in Year 5?
faq.a: Start with a number line to show which multiple is closer, then teach the rule: look one place to the right. Practise halfway numbers and 9s that round up, such as 695,000 to 700,000, and use rounding to estimate.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 300,000 when you round to the nearest 100,000?
items.e: Numbers from 250,000 to 349,999 round to 300,000. 249,999 has 4 ten thousands, so it rounds down to 200,000. The smallest is 250,000.

items.q: What is the greatest whole number that rounds to 80,000 when you round to the nearest 10,000?

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 63,700 when you round to the nearest 100?

items.q: Round 645,380 to the nearest 10,000 and to the nearest 100,000. Which pair is correct?
items.e: Always round the number you started with, 645,380. Nearest 10,000: the thousands digit is 5, so 650,000. Nearest 100,000: the ten thousands digit is 4, so 600,000. Do not round 650,000 again to get 700,000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 386,000 to the nearest 1,000 and to 390,000 to the nearest 10,000?
items.e: Numbers from 385,500 to 386,499 round to 386,000. Only 385,740 is in that range, and it rounds to 390,000 because its thousands digit is 5. 386,600 rounds to 387,000.

items.q: Estimate 48,750 + 31,260 by rounding each number to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 48,750 rounds to 49,000 and 31,260 rounds to 31,000. 49,000 + 31,000 = 80,000. (The exact answer is 80,010, so the estimate is close.)

items.q: George works out 38,460 + 24,915 and gets 53,375. Round each number to the nearest 1,000 to estimate the answer. What is the estimate?
items.e: 38,460 rounds to 38,000 and 24,915 rounds to 25,000. 38,000 + 25,000 = 63,000. (The exact answer is 63,375, so the estimate is close.) George’s answer is too far from 63,000, so it must be wrong.

items.q: About 400,000 people live in a city, rounded to the nearest 100,000. What is the greatest number of people who could live there?
items.e: Numbers from 350,000 to 449,999 round to 400,000. 450,000 rounds up to 500,000, so the greatest is 449,999.

items.q: A poster says the Moon is about 400,000 km away. The real distance is 384,400 km. What was it rounded to?
items.e: To the nearest 100,000, 384,400 rounds up to 400,000. To the nearest 10,000 it is 380,000, and to the nearest 1,000 it is 384,000.
